extracted.intended_audience: Users of the SINGULAR computer algebra system (mathematicians / computational algebraists) working on plane curve and hypersurface singularities
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for SINGULAR library procedures (equising.lib, gmssing.lib, gmspoly.lib, hnoether.lib) describing usage, preconditions/assumptions, returned data structures and examples for computing equisingularity strata, Hamburger–Noether expansions, Gauss–Manin invariants, spectra, monodromy, and related invariants.

rubrics_metrics.name: esStratum output format
rubrics_metrics.description: Output of 'esStratum' is a list whose first component(s) encode ideals defining the equisingularity stratum and the part where all equimultiple sections are trivial; examples show entries like _[1][1] = ideal defining the equisingularity stratum and _[1][2] = ideal defining the part where all equimultiple sections are trivial. The second component often equals 0 when there is no nontrivial part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The procedure prints progress messages (HN expansion, blowup steps, elimination, removal of superfluous equations). printlevel>=2 displays additional information. The list entries shown in examples illustrate how coefficients/relations (e.g., _[1]=g, _[2]=f, _[3]=b, _[4]=a, _[5]=...) appear; users should inspect M[1], M[2] etc. See also esIdeal and isEquising references.

rubrics_metrics.name: isEquising preconditions and return
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: isEquising(F[,m,L]); F poly, m int, L list. Assume F defines a deformation of a reduced bivariate polynomial f and the characteristic of the basering does not divide mult(f). If nv is the number of variables of the basering, the first nv-2 variables are the deformation parameters. If the basering is a qring, ideal(basering) must only depend on the deformation parameters. L is supposed to be the output of hnexpansion (with the given ordering of the variables appearing in f). If m is given, the family is considered over A/maxideal(m).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return value: int 1 if the family is equisingular along the trivial section, 0 otherwise. The procedure uses execute (or calls a procedure using execute). printlevel>=2 displays additional information. Examples illustrate calling isEquising on examples and on computation over Q[a,b]/<a,b>^2. Ensure hnexpansion output ordering matches variable ordering in f.

rubrics_metrics.name: controlMatrix (multsequence output interpretation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume L is the output of multsequence(hnexpansion(f)). Return list M of 4 intmat’s: M[1] contains multiplicities at respective infinitely near points p[i,j] with a storage rule when multiple branches pass through same point; M[2] contains number of branches meeting at p[i,j]; M[3] contains splitting information of M[1][i,j] w.r.t. different tangents (stored only for minimal j>=k corresponding to a new tangent direction); M[4] contains maximal sum of higher multiplicities for a branch passing through p[i,j] (= degree bound for blowing up).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: branches are ordered so only consecutive branches can meet at an infinitely near point. Final rows of M[1]..M[3] are (1,1,1,...) corresponding to smooth strict transforms meeting the exceptional divisor transversally. See multsequence for relation to hnexpansion output.

rubrics_metrics.name: gmssing.lib purpose and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose: library for computing invariants related to the Gauss-Manin system of an isolated hypersurface singularity (monodromy, Bernstein–Sato polynomial, spectrum, spectral pairs, V-filtration, etc.). Assumes isolation of critical point and characteristic 0 in many procedures. References to Schulze papers and background theory are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures compute differential and Hodge-theoretic invariants; see cross-references to dmod.lib, gmspoly.lib, mondromy.lib, spectrum.lib for related functionality.

rubrics_metrics.name: gmsring usage and return
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: gmsring(t,s); poly t, string s. Assume characteristic 0; local degree ordering; isolated critical point 0 of t. Return: ring G; Gauss-Manin system of t with variable s. Also sets gmspoly=t; gmsjacob (Jacobian ideal), gmsstd (standard basis of Jacobian ideal), gmsmatrix (matrix relating Jacobian ideal to standard basis), gmsbasis (monomial vector space basis of Jacobian algebra), and int Gmssing::gmsmaxdeg (maximal weight of variables).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows how to call gmsring and inspect gmsjacob, gmsstd, gmsmatrix, gmsbasis, and gmsmaxdeg. Use setring(G) to work in returned ring.

rubrics_metrics.name: gmsnf projection normal form (gmsnf)
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: gmsnf(p,K); poly p, int K. Assume basering returned by gmsring. Return: list nf with nf[1] = projection of p to <gmsbasis>C[[s]] mod s^(K+1), nf[2] such that p == nf[1] + nf[2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computation can be continued by setting p = nf[2]. Examples illustrate iterative use for increasing K and recovering series expansion terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: gmscoeffs basis coefficients (gmscoeffs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: gmscoeffs(p,K); poly p, int K. Assume basering constructed by gmsring. Return: list l where l[1] is matrix representing p in C[[s]]-basis mod s^(K+1) and l[2] is ideal with p == matrix(gmsbasis)*l[1] + l[2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computation can be continued by setting p = l[2]. Examples show coefficient vectors and a trailing 1/2*s term when K=1.

rubrics_metrics.name: bernstein returns Bernstein–Sato polynomial
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: bernstein(t); poly t. Assume characteristic 0; local degree ordering; isolated critical point 0 of t. Return: list bs where bs[1] is Bernstein–Sato polynomial b(s) (ideal) and bs[2] is an intvec of multiplicities of its roots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example prints roots like -13/10,-11/10,... and multiplicities vector like 1,1,2,1,1,2. Use to obtain b(s) and root multiplicities.

rubrics_metrics.name: monodromy returns Jordan data of monodromy matrix
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: monodromy(t); poly t. Assume characteristic 0; local degree ordering; isolated critical point 0 of t. Return: list l containing Jordan data of monodromy matrix exp(-2*pi*i*M): l[1] ideal of eigenvalues (numbers), l[2] intvec sizes of Jordan blocks, l[3] intvec multiplicities of each Jordan block.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show eigenvalues and associated block sizes and multiplicities. Cross-reference to linalg and mondromy libraries for related matrix operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: spectrum returns singularity spectrum
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: spectrum(t); poly t. Assume characteristic 0; local degree ordering; isolated critical point 0 of t. Return: list sp where sp[1] is ideal of spectral numbers and sp[2] is intvec of multiplicities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: spprint or spprint-like helpers format output; example shows spectral numbers with multiplicities, e.g., (-1/2,1),(-3/10,2),.... See spectrum.lib for more.

rubrics_metrics.name: sppairs returns spectral pairs
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: sppairs(t); poly t. Assume characteristic 0; local degree ordering; isolated critical point 0 of t. Return: list spp where spp[1] ideal lists V-filtration indices, spp[2] intvec weight filtration indices, spp[3] intvec multiplicities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sppprint to display spectral pairs. Example output uses pairs like ((-1/2,2),1),((-3/10,1),2),... See spectrum.lib cross-reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: vfilt returns the V-filtration on H''/s*H''
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: vfilt(t); poly t. Assume characteristic 0; local degree ordering; isolated critical point 0 of t. Return: list v where v[1] numbers are V-filtration indices, v[2] multiplicities, v[3] list of modules for graded parts, v[4] monomial vector space basis of H''/s*H'', and v[5] standard basis of Jacobian ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows v[4] listing monomial basis elements (y5,y4,...,1) and v[5] standard basis entries; use endvfilt to translate to Jacobian algebra filtration.

rubrics_metrics.name: vwfilt returns weighted V-filtration
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: vwfilt(t); poly t. Assume characteristic 0; local degree ordering; isolated critical point 0 of t. Return: list vw with vw[1] V-filtration indices of spectral pairs, vw[2] weight filtration indices, vw[3] multiplicities, vw[4] modules for graded parts, vw[5] monomial basis of H''/s*H'', vw[6] standard basis of Jacobian ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows how weighted indices and multiplicities are returned and how monomial bases and Jacobian standard bases are included.

rubrics_metrics.name: tmatrix returns A0,A1,T,M encoding differential operation
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: tmatrix(t); poly t. Assume characteristic 0; local degree ordering; isolated critical point 0 of t. Return: list l = A0,A1,T,M where A0,A1 are matrices (A(s)=A0+s*A1 and t[matrix(b)] = [matrix(b)](A(s)+s^2*(d/ds))), T is C-basis module, M is monomial C-basis of H''/sH''.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows printed matrices and basis M (y5,...,1). Use jet and print to inspect the matrices; output encodes differential structure of Gauss–Manin system.

rubrics_metrics.name: endvfilt obtains V-filtration on Jacobian algebra
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: endvfilt(v); list v (where v returned by vfilt). Return: list ev containing V-filtration on the Jacobian algebra: ev[1] ideal of V-filtration indices, ev[2] intvec multiplicities, ev[3] list of modules for graded parts, ev[4] monomial basis of Jacobian algebra, ev[5] standard basis of Jacobian ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows resulting V-filtration indices like 0,1/5,2/5,... and monomial basis mapping to Jacobian algebra gens. Use after vfilt to convert H''/s*H'' data to Jacobian algebra context.

rubrics_metrics.name: sppnf orders spectral pairs with multiplicity
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: sppnf(list(a,w[,m])); ideal a, intvec w, intvec m. Assume ncols(a) == size(w) == size(m). Return: ordered spectral pairs (a[i],w[i]) with multiplicity m[i] lexicographically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sppprint to format output. Example demonstrates conversion to grouped (value,multiplicity) tuples.

rubrics_metrics.name: sppprint formats spectral pairs
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: sppprint(spp); list spp. Return: string s containing formatted spectral pairs for human-readable display.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows output format ((-1/2,2),1),((-3/10,1),2),... Use for printing spp from sppairs or sppnf.

rubrics_metrics.name: spadd sums spectra
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: spadd(sp1,sp2); list sp1, list sp2. Return: list sp representing the sum of spectra sp1 and sp2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates additive merging of spectral numbers and multiplicities; use spprint to display the result.

rubrics_metrics.name: spsub subtracts spectra
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: spsub(sp1,sp2); list sp1, list sp2. Return: list sp representing the difference of spectra sp1 and sp2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows that multiplicities can become negative if subtraction yields that; inspect results carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: spmul scales/combines spectra linearly
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: spmul(sp0,k); list sp0, int[vec] k. Return: list sp which is linear combination of spectra sp0 with coefficients k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show doubling a spectrum (k=2) or combining multiple spectra with integer coefficients; use to generate linear combinations in deformation arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: spissemicont semicontinuity test for spectrum sums
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: spissemicont(sp[,1]); list sp, int opt. Return: int indicating whether sum of sp is positive on all intervals [a,a+1) (1) or negative on some interval (0), depending on option.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates checking positivity/negativity of sums on unit intervals; used to test semicontinuity conditions in deformation contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: spsemicont computes semicontinuity bounds for occurrences in deformations
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: spsemicont(sp0,sp,k[,1]); list sp0, list sp. Return: list l of intvecs l[i] giving upper bounds l[i] such that multiplicities k of spectra sp0 occurring in a deformation with spectrum sp satisfy k <= l[i].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows computing l and then testing with spissemicont to verify borderline cases; used to determine how many copies of given spectra can occur in deformations.

rubrics_metrics.name: spmilnor computes Milnor number from spectrum
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: spmilnor(sp); list sp. Return: int mu, the Milnor number of spectrum sp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: spmilnor returns 11 for a sample spectrum. Use as invariant check for computed spectra.

rubrics_metrics.name: spgeomgenus computes geometric genus from spectrum
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: spgeomgenus(sp); list sp. Return: int g, the geometric genus of spectrum sp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example returns 6 for a sample spectrum. Use as Hodge-theoretic invariant derived from spectral data.

rubrics_metrics.name: spgamma computes gamma invariant from spectrum
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: spgamma(sp); list sp. Return: number gamma, the gamma invariant of spectrum sp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: spgamma returns 1/240 for a sample spectrum. Use for fine invariants related to spectral distributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: isTame test for tame polynomials (gmspoly.lib)
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: isTame(f); poly f. Assume basering has no variables named w(1),w(2),... Return: int 1 if f is tame in the sense of Broughton, 0 otherwise. Procedure implements Proposition 3.1 in Broughton [Bro88].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: isTame(x2*y+x) -> 0; isTame(x3+y3+xy) -> 1. Use to check cohomological tameness prerequisites before invoking goodBasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: goodBasis computes a good basis of the Brieskorn lattice
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: goodBasis(f); poly f. Assume f is cohomologically tame (Sabbah). Return: ring R (basering with new variable s), ideal b, matrix A where A(s)=A0+s*A1 and t[matrix(b)] = [matrix(b)](A(s)+s^2*(d/ds)), and [matrix(b)] is a good basis of the Brieskorn lattice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implements Algorithm 6 in Schulze [Sch05]. Example shows returned basis elements b[i] and jets of A; use setring(Rs) to inspect outputs. Use only for tame polynomials.

rubrics_metrics.name: hnexpansion (Hamburger–Noether expansion) usage and returns
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: hnexpansion(f[,"ess"]); f poly. Assume f is a bivariate polynomial in the first two ring variables. Return: list L containing Hamburger–Noether (HN) data of f: for each branch L[i] is a list with L[i][1] matrix of HNE lines (rows are coefficient lists), L[i][2] intvec of line lengths, L[i][3] int flag (0 if first variable transversal, 1 if variables were changed, -1 if error), L[i][4] transformed equation of the i-th branch (or 0). If computation required a field extension, L[1] may be a ring containing stored hne and polynomial f; when called with "ess" only one representative per conjugacy class is computed and L[2] is an intvec giving multiplicities of conjugacy classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If f is irreducible as a power series, consider develop(f) instead. Increasing printlevel yields more comments; defining HNDebugOn yields maximum comments. Examples show parameterizations and handling of field extensions (QQ[a]/(a^2+1)). Use displayHNE, param, and related helpers to view expansions.

rubrics_metrics.name: develop (HN expansion for irreducible f)
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: develop(f [,n]); f poly, n int. Assume f is a bivariate polynomial in first two variables and irreducible as power series (use hnexpansion for reducible f). Return: list L with L[1] matrix of HNE rows, L[2] intvec indicating lengths, L[3] int flag (0 transversal, 1 variables changed, -1 error), L[4] transformed polynomial for extension, L[5] int 1 if curve has exactly one branch (irreducible) else 0. The procedure displays (non-zero) elements of the HNE unless called by another procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional n affects only computation of the LAST line of the HNE: if given, HN-matrix will have at least n columns. If n negative, algorithm stops when invariants(L) suffices, but last line may be incomplete and marked with the 2nd variable. For speed, use basering ordering ls. printlevel>=0 displays comments. Examples show how to interpret the HN matrix, param() warnings about truncation, and displayHNE.

rubrics_metrics.name: extdevelop extends HN development to more terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: extdevelop(L,N); list L, int N. Assume L is output of develop(f) or of extdevelop(l,n) or an hne entry in a ring created by hnexpansion. Return: extension of the Hamburger–Noether development of f in same format as develop output (up to last entry). The new HN-matrix will have at least N columns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In particular, extdevelop(develop(f),N) will (in most cases) produce same result as develop(f,N) for irreducible f. If matrix M of L has n columns, param(extdevelop(L,N)) increases exactness by at least (N-n) more significant monomials. Use to refine parametrization/truncation accuracy.
